name: New Nationalism
summary: New Nationalism is the Progressive programme of Theodore Roosevelt, drawing on Herbert Croly, that uses a strong federal government and executive to regulate large corporations, protect workers and put human welfare ahead of property rights. It accepts industrial concentration but wants it supervised by expert commissions, with democratic reforms such as primaries, initiative, referendum and recall to keep government answerable to the people rather than to business and party bosses.
scope: The American programme of Roosevelt's 1910 Osawatomie speech and the 1912 Progressive (Bull Moose) platform, with Croly's The Promise of American Life as its intellectual base. It excludes the later general sense of nationalism and Roosevelt's wider imperial record, and many modern issues are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Roosevelt called for a national health service consolidating federal medical agencies and the platform urged social insurance against sickness, but neither amounted to universal state-guaranteed care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The platform sought minimum wage standards for working women and a living wage in all industrial occupations, though not a general substantial raise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Roosevelt held that markets and large combinations needed federal commissions to supervise them, rejecting laissez-faire as sufficient.

public-ownership.rationale: He wanted regulation of corporations by commissions, not nationalization; only water power and natural resources were to stay publicly owned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The platform backed a graduated inheritance tax and the income tax amendment, moving taxes toward the wealthy without demanding sweeping hikes.

unions-good.rationale: The platform favoured organization of workers, men and women, and a cabinet Labor Department, while condemning labor violence.

property-fundamental.rationale: Roosevelt said every man holds property subject to the community's right to regulate its use and that he was for men over property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Strong federal regulation of interstate corporations by an administrative commission was the signature plank of the program.

cut-welfare.rationale: The platform proposed social insurance for the sick, old and unemployed, the opposite of cutting welfare, though Roosevelt opposed handouts to those who refuse to work.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the speeches proposes worker-owned firms; the program relied on regulation and cooperation of employers and labor within private enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The sources do not touch surveillance; a strong-state nationalist might accept it but progressives were also concerned with civil rights, so it is split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a moralistic Progressive Era reformer of 1912 would be expected to disfavour recreational drug legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents of the era had no developed position on legally restricting hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Roosevelt called the presidency the steward of the public welfare and said strong leadership was needed against party bosses, but he spoke of leading, not bypassing, the people.

state-harmful.rationale: The whole programme holds that a strong national government is the necessary instrument of justice and welfare.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Roosevelt was a hunter and gun enthusiast but his program had no gun plank.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform sought a modest navy buildup and a small well-run army, not broad new police or military authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Progressive reformers of the era sought to protect women and children from exploitation, suggesting opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: At Osawatomie Roosevelt said problems beyond the states can be handled only by the nation, but the Progressive platform also pressed state-level reforms, so he did not reject local decision-making as such.

rehabilitation.rationale: The sources do not discuss prisons; Progressive Era reform favoured rehabilitation but Roosevelt also emphasized firmness against crime.

traditional-family.rationale: Roosevelt stressed family life and the role of mothers in raising healthy children, though family structure was not an issue he legislated on.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not an issue in 1912; inferred from the era's conventional views and Roosevelt's emphasis on traditional family life.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Roosevelt's strong pro-natalist, family-centred rhetoric.

more-religion-public.rationale: The programme is secular in content; Roosevelt used moral language but proposed no larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The sources do not address race and progressives were divided on racial justice, so adherents are genuinely split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Roosevelt backed equality of right but not identical functions for the sexes; the concept was not available in 1912.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The program stressed assimilation and education of immigrants into American national life as part of a unified national community.

gradual-change.rationale: Roosevelt wanted substantial reform including limits on courts and easier amendments, yet defended orderly change against mob action.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform proposed distributing and assimilating immigrants, not cutting numbers; restriction was not its plank.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The platform's foreign policy was nationalist, with naval limitation by agreement but no supranational authority; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Roosevelt opposed a revenue-only tariff and backed protection that benefits workers, with an expert commission to set rates.

nation-first.rationale: The ideology is nationalist, concentrating on national welfare, though the platform also sought naval limitation and open commerce.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed in 1912 sources; Roosevelt's wider record was interventionist but the programme itself is silent.

open-borders.rationale: The platform wanted immigrants distributed and assimilated under supervision, inconsistent with eventual open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Roosevelt championed conservation of resources and public use but never proposed limits on economic growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the conservation programme suggests sympathy for environmental protection but not climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; Progressive faith in expertise suggests optimism, but sources give no statement about technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates 1912 and the programme never mentions energy technology, so no position can be inferred beyond its general support for public-benefit resource policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Roosevelt condemned lawless mob violence as strongly as corporate greed and framed progressivism as reform within constitutional order.

experts-over-public.rationale: The program relied on expert commissions yet paired them with initiative, referendum and primaries to give the people the final word.

central-planning.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt wanted supervision and some planning of a private economy, not a centrally planned one.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the program accepts private business under regulation, not worker or public ownership as a condition.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not in the program, which favoured graduated income and inheritance taxes instead.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The speech and platform explicitly call for a graduated inheritance tax as a central plank.

basic-income.rationale: The program offered social insurance and a living wage tied to work, and Roosevelt opposed aid to those who refuse to work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform supports protective tariff tied to workers' living standards, with unjust schedules revised downward by commission.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Federal commissions would supervise capitalization of corporations, but directing investment to strategic industries was not proposed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Roosevelt favoured settlers and small farmers over exploitation of resources, and sought to curb concentration's political power.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme demanded a living wage and shorter hours inside the wage system.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The speech called for a revamped financial system under national authority; abolition was not contemplated.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Roosevelt favoured worker combination and an industrial commission, but not state-recognized bodies setting wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Progressive platform sought a more democratic system with primaries and attacked party bosses, rejecting single-party control.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Roosevelt and the platform held to republican government by the people, with no hereditary role.

democracy-best.rationale: The platform opens with government by a self-controlled democracy and extends popular rule by primaries, initiative and recall.

direct-votes.rationale: The platform urged initiative and referendum, and Roosevelt backed them where representative government has failed.

workers-councils.rationale: Nothing suggests councils as a basis of power; the program works through the existing representative state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nationalism holds the Union indivisible and stresses national over sectional authority.

natural-rulers.rationale: The program is democratic and attacks privilege, though Croly respected leadership by exceptional individuals.

political-violence-never.rationale: Roosevelt condemned mob violence and labor violence but defended force in war and law enforcement, so it is split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Roosevelt personally prized the strenuous life, yet the 1912 sources do not endorse war as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1912 platform and Roosevelt's speeches are silent on church and state, so this is left at neutral as an unaddressed question.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The programme is a secular legislative agenda of social justice grounded in welfare and democracy, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: National government should hold regulatory and defence authority; Roosevelt wanted stronger public agencies.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform backed building two battleships a year until an international naval-limitation agreement, a strong but not supremacist stance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement spoke of American nationality through assimilation, not ethnic homogeneity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Roosevelt condemned both corporate greed and class violence and Croly sought national unity above class interest.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Roosevelt wanted every worthy person to have a chance, which is opportunity rather than equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a centralizing nationalism with no indigenous-sovereignty plank.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; inferred from national-interest orientation.

civilizational-union.rationale: The New Nationalism is about uniting one American nation behind federal action, and nothing in it envisions union with other nations by shared civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt saw individual self-interest as a source of greed and corruption to be checked by civic duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Croly's New Nationalism rested on duty to others and civic virtue, a constructive individualism, over older individualism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The conservation programme valued resources for public benefit, though Roosevelt also loved wilderness; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Roosevelt's rhetoric prized large families, so population limits would be opposed; not in sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme accepted industrial concentration as natural and sought to regulate it, not reverse it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; Progressive reform favoured orderly institutions over disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Biotechnological enhancement lies far outside the 1912 programme, which addressed wages, trusts and democracy; no stance can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; Progressive faith in expert commissions only loosely relates.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for this early-twentieth-century programme, which says nothing on state access to private communication.

restore-past-order.rationale: Progressive nationalism looks forward, with Hamiltonian means for new problems, and sees old individualism as outdated.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt used pragmatic means to secure ends; Roosevelt said to judge by the human welfare they achieve.

direct-action.rationale: The programme sought change through elections, primaries, and legislation, and condemned mob violence.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a theme of the sources; Croly justified strong means for democratic ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Roosevelt and Croly accepted industrial concentration as a permanent, natural development to be regulated, so a return to foraging is firmly rejected by inference.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Nothing in the sources approaches this; the programme accepts the industrial economy with better wages and hours.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Roosevelt wanted wages above the bare cost of living and a chance for worthy people, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme left production to private profit-seeking firms under federal supervision, so production purely for need rather than profit is not its position.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Roosevelt ranked dividends below human character but defended legitimate profit and rejected class-war views.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The programme is cross-class and condemns violence by workers as well as employers, which clearly rejects class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme backed small farmers, cooperative marketing and farm relief, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of the programme; it endorsed regulated capitalism and foreign commerce.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme proposes new taxes on income and inheritance to fund government and justice.

harm-principle.rationale: The program justifies restricting property and conduct for the public welfare, going beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Croly emphasized social obligation and the community's right to regulate property.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the platform wanted a small well-run army, not conscription, but Roosevelt's nationalism accepts national service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme is built on strengthening the vote through primaries, initiative and recall.

state-as-business.rationale: The program saw government as steward of public welfare, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The programme held that welfare, a living wage and a chance underpin real freedom, consistent with Croly's Jeffersonian ends.

media-academia-power.rationale: The programme's complaint was business domination of politics, not control by media or universities; the claim is not part of it, so it leans against.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Roosevelt's era held some such views but the programme did not address it and sources are silent.

organic-representation.rationale: The platform relies on direct election, primaries and referendums rather than corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Roosevelt wanted regulation for social justice while defending private property and individual character, which rules out a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not defining; Croly sought national renewal through reform, but not radical rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The platform is silent on expansion; Roosevelt's other record was expansionist but the 1912 programme was not.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The platform's plank on rule by the people and its attack on party bosses clearly oppose authority built on personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Roosevelt's labour protections and settler-friendly land policy clearly oppose tying farmers to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Croly's pragmatic Progressive faith in expert investigation assumes knowable facts, so a power-relativist view of knowledge is not part of the programme; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Roosevelt appealed to character, justice and human welfare as shared moral standards.

single-common-good.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt held that national interest and public welfare should override special interests and class interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is not addressed in the sources and the New Nationalism is an American domestic reform programme, so no position is inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in the programme and cannot be inferred from its domestic reform focus.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is unrelated to this American programme, which does not address language policy at all.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The platform backed workers' organization and regulation, not a vote on running companies.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme backed public institutions and rural education suited to country life, so publicly funded private school choice is inferred as unwelcome.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Deficit stimulus doctrine postdates the programme, whose fiscal planks were income and inheritance taxes, so adherents had no developed view.

economic-freedom.rationale: Roosevelt held that unchecked economic freedom threatens democracy, and wanted business regulated.

rule-by-example.rationale: Roosevelt valued character and example but his programme was a long list of new laws and commissions, so he did not rely on example over law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from the name and nationalist framing; the programme says nothing about every nation's right to its own state.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; a nationalist programme keeps freedom of action, but the sources do not discuss it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The programme gives no ruling on faith versus reason; Roosevelt's rhetoric mixed moral appeal with pragmatic expertise, so it is neutral.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; assimilation of immigrants was a plank but no welfare distinctions.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Roosevelt supported a chance for every worthy person, not handouts to those who refuse to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt rejected class conflict and sought cooperation of labor and capital under national oversight.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalist respect for American institutions and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of non-Western dominated nations is foreign to the programme, which concerns American domestic reform and national power.

workers-nation.rationale: The programme sought national unity and workers' integration into national life rather than international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Roosevelt backed equal suffrage while denying identical functions; law distinguished women for protective labor legislation.

ban-interest.rationale: The speech wanted a revamped national financial system but never questioned lending at interest, so a legal ban is rejected by inference.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The programme did not address race; Roosevelt's wider record was inconsistent and sources are silent.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The programme saw the state as steward of the public welfare, above class interest.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; conservation programme would restrain exploitation but no fossil fuel position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The 1912 platform pledged to promote the education and assimilation of immigrants, closely supervising agencies serving them.

elite-replacement.rationale: The platform wanted immigrants distributed and assimilated, treating them as future Americans; it holds no replacement conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: The programme's electoral reforms were primaries, the short ballot and direct election of senators; proportional systems are not mentioned.

national-mission.rationale: Croly spoke of national promise but the 1912 programme does not call for spreading government abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The programme backed women's suffrage and protection but not a theory of structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Roosevelt attacked party bosses and the plunder league of professional politicians and sought to dissolve the alliance of corrupt business and politics, though he blamed machines rather than all elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Progressive Era eugenics sympathies existed but are not documented here.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources do not discuss transitional justice for past security-force abuses, so adherents have no defined view.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme was explicitly for a strong federal government regulating the economy and providing social protection.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The sources do not discuss intermarriage, and Progressive adherents were divided on race, so it is left neutral with low confidence.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Roosevelt's rhetoric stressed a chance for every worthy man and equality of right, though race was a division among progressives.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal debate within Marxism-Leninism, and the New Nationalism rejected socialism, so it has no stake in the question.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The programme celebrates American national promise and does not frame the United States as a colonial project; inferred opposition.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The programme wanted national uniform standards for labor and commerce but never discussed religion and personal law, so it leans mildly in favour by analogy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Roosevelt's American liberal Protestant milieu would oppose legal limits on conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A cattle slaughter ban has no basis in the programme, whose meat-related interest was federal inspection and regulation of industry.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in public schools is not covered in the platform or speeches, so adherents had no stated position.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Soviet-era doctrine irrelevant to the programme; no position can be inferred except general support for state strength.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The platform insists government rest on the rule of the people with the people having final authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: The platform backed foreign commerce with government cooperation but did not articulate a trade-surplus aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Nothing in the platform or Roosevelt's speeches proposes forcing minorities out; its immigrant plank was assimilation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The programme justifies coercive regulation, taxation and limits on property for the public welfare, so an absolute non-aggression rule is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Roosevelt prized the strenuous life, yet the 1912 programme stressed cooperation and regulation of unrestrained competition; the sources give no direct statement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banning parties is not discussed; Roosevelt condemned violence but the programme focused on reform of parties through primaries rather than outlawing them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The goal of ending domination of government by business and bosses parallels this idea, though the republican theory is not cited by the sources; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Roosevelt wanted a stronger executive and curtailed court power while keeping constitutional order, so adherents are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The programme seeks reform through elections and legislation, which clearly runs against a revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme gave priority to human welfare over property and sought to protect workers, women and children.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British issue and the 1912 American programme says nothing on public housing sales.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The platform proposed limiting court injunctions in strikes yet condemned labor violence.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme located hardship in industrial conditions, low wages and corporate power, not in population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The programme did not discuss diversity directly; its stress on assimilation suggests concern for cohesion but not a claim about diversity itself.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lottery selection contradicts the programme's reliance on primaries, election and recall to hold officials accountable.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The programme's constitutional-reform spirit and its concern with lawless mob violence give no support for suspending legal protections, though it is not addressed directly.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on foods are not in the programme, which addressed tariffs and trust regulation rather than direct price-fixing.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme demanded publicity of campaign contributions and committee proceedings, the opposite of party control over information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Roosevelt's program had the army and navy serve the nation under constitutional civil authority, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the platform, which focused on assimilation and distribution of immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislator pay is not mentioned; Roosevelt's reforms focused on campaign finance and bars on corporate compensation of officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Roosevelt condemned bosses and the machine and urged direct primaries, so binding party discipline is disfavoured.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The programme's foreign policy is nationalist, seeking naval limitation by agreement but no transfer of sovereignty to supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president as commander in chief is standard; Roosevelt wanted a strong executive.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a concern of this political programme, so there is no stated view.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule is foreign to the secular democratic programme resting on the rule of the people.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is incompatible with the programme's nationalism and its commitment to a strong navy and national defense.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Art censorship is not covered; Roosevelt prized moral character but the programme proposed no censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Roosevelt himself ran for a third term but the programme took no position; split with leaning against.

recall-officials.rationale: The platform and Roosevelt's speech explicitly endorse recall and easy removal of unfaithful officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The United States held no permanent military alliances in 1912 and the platform did not discuss them; adherents have no clear view.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rental housing is not in the programme, which proposed tenement manufacturing limits but accepted private property markets.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform sought a small, well-run army and a regularly built navy, not a replacement of professional forces with armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Roosevelt valued the farmer and rural education but also industrial progress.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification of divided peoples is not addressed in this American domestic programme.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Progressive movement prized expertise and learning and had no anti-university theme.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The programme does not discuss cultural relativism, and the era's nationalism generally assumed hierarchy between civilizations; inferred lean against.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not addressed in the platform or speeches, so no position is documented.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not addressed in the 1912 programme.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; the Progressive embrace of science and modern expertise suggests opposition to teaching creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law is not in the programme, so no stance is documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: American nationality in the programme is civic, assimilationist rather than by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme promoted assimilation and education of immigrants into American national life, not state support of minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws for religious minorities are not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Roosevelt stressed civic character and duty over individual eccentricity, so he is unlikely to endorse this Millian claim; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debt relief is not addressed by the programme and cannot be firmly inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial independence debates are foreign to this programme; no position.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Roosevelt wanted easier constitutional amendment and popular override of court decisions but did not propose rewriting the constitution through an assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The platform expanded political rights through suffrage, primaries and recall and offers no support for suspending freedoms for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not in the platform, whose foreign planks were naval strength, commerce and the Panama Canal.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic to a 1912 programme that cannot take a position on them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The platform backed presidential primaries and direct election of senators, extending direct popular choice.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The speech wanted a revamped national financial system under democratic authority, and Progressive thinkers distrusted insulation from public control, though no central bank plank is documented.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions for peace are not addressed in the programme.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Roosevelt said property is held subject to the community's right to regulate its use and he ranked human welfare above it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The debate about the Soviet Union postdates the programme, so it has no position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The precautionary principle postdates the programme; its conservation plank suggests concern for resources but no stated principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defense treaties are not addressed in the platform, whose foreign policy sought naval limitation and honorable dealing.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses the status of annexed territory, so no stance is inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The programme is silent on curbing church power and property, so it has no stated position.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The program wanted a president who leads the people, not a ceremonial figure.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not directly addressed, but the Nationalist stress on the indivisible national union implies force may be used to preserve it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The programme stressed uniform national standards over regional differences and thus leans against one country, two systems arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The programme rests on popular government and attacks on bosses, which clearly rules out a sacred head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The platform called for a graduated inheritance tax and the income tax amendment, treating progressive rates as fair.

character-from-environment.rationale: Roosevelt emphasized individual character but also saw social conditions as shaping lives.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Roosevelt's program sought reforms to hold officials and corporations accountable.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic for a 1912 programme.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed constitution theory is not referenced, and the programme emphasized the people's rule within the American system, so it is neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Roosevelt wanted leadership that leads, not drives, and attacked the machine, so cult-like honours for the leader are not part of the programme.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class struggle under socialism is a Marxist-Leninist debate with no relevance for the programme.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme favoured settlers and small farmers on public land but not taking large estates from their owners.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not addressed in the programme.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims to territory abroad based on co-nationals are not part of this programme, whose nationalism is civic and domestic.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the programme's secular democratic framework; religious law is never discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering has no basis in the programme, which backed women's suffrage and equality of right.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union across states is not discussed in the programme.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are foreign to the programme, which defines nationalism around one American state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The programme promoted assimilation into a common American culture, not minority self-governing institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The issue of minorities staying versus emigrating is not addressed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not a theme of the programme; Roosevelt and Croly gave weight to ideals, character and politics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Roosevelt said to penalize conduct, not size, and accepted large combinations under regulation, while strengthening the Sherman Law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed, though the programme's federal financial oversight would not oppose public rescue on principle, so it is left neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Roosevelt wanted the people to hold final authority and to be able to reverse court decisions, curbing judicial power.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The programme backed women's suffrage but never proposed quotas for public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The platform sought expanded foreign commerce with government cooperation, which rules out a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Roosevelt pushed domestic labor and conservation standards but trade agreements with binding standards are anachronistic, so no position.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral over material incentives is a socialist-state theme not found in the programme, which sought living wages.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco-style revolution is incompatible with the programme's condemnation of lawless violence and its electoral reform path.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme attacked special interests and privilege and sought an inheritance tax.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist education stresses the national past, and Roosevelt's emphasis on Americanism supports history centred on one's own nation; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Roosevelt's wider record included tutelage but 1912 programme does not address.

patriotic-education.rationale: The platform's emphasis on education and assimilation into American life supports teaching civic loyalty and national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are anachronistic for 1912 and unaddressed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Roosevelt called for a revamped financial system but did not propose public money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The programme's premise is that regulation lets capitalism adapt and avoid class conflict and collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence in former imperial regions is not part of the programme.

delink-world-market.rationale: The platform sought expanded foreign commerce, so delinking from the world market is contrary to the programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the thesis is Marxist and the programme, which never discusses it, takes the gains of trade as legitimate.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, but a programme committed to regulating business for human welfare is unlikely to give owners unlimited freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Roosevelt wanted constitutional amendment easier and courts less able to block social laws.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaties are not addressed in the programme.

elective-rulers.rationale: The programme is a republican one built around election, primaries and popular control of government.

minority-veto.rationale: The programme was majoritarian, giving the people final authority and curtailing court power, so a minority veto is rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resisting rulers who break the law is not discussed; Roosevelt stressed lawful reform and recall of unfaithful officials, so it is neutral.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is a British debate; the programme worked within American separated powers and a strong presidency.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare was not part of the programme, though Roosevelt as a naturalist cared for wildlife; no stance documented.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Roosevelt was a hunter and conservationist who accepted use of animals within sportsmanlike limits; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Croly's New Nationalism grounded politics in duty to others and Roosevelt cast officials and the wealthy as stewards of the public welfare.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The programme demanded citizen participation through primaries and recall, and Roosevelt prized civic engagement over withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not part of the programme.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Cultural hegemony is a Gramscian idea outside the programme, which denied a single ruling class.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is outside the programme.

native-born-offices.rationale: The programme did not propose reserving offices to the native-born, and the platform treated immigrants as future citizens to be assimilated.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party autonomy is irrelevant to the programme.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Foreign aid and development are not addressed in the programme.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not part of the programme.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political leadership is not addressed, and the programme's civic nationalism would not endorse it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism postdates the programme, so it cannot be inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The sources do not address Civil War causation, so adherents have no stated position; Roosevelt's era of Republicans generally credited slavery, so inferred lean against.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument controversies are anachronistic and not in the programme.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage is not addressed in the programme, which was concerned with working women and children.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Roosevelt and Croly were committed to American democratic institutions and the programme does not cast them as civilization-specific; no stated view.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The programme kept the army under civil authority and sought a small one, so a political guardian role is not part of it.

paid-care-work.rationale: Roosevelt valued mothers' role in raising healthy children but proposed no payment for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is not discussed, though family life was praised; neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service reform was a Progressive concern, but the sources do not call for filling posts by examination instead of election.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign takeovers are not discussed in the programme.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed; Roosevelt's family emphasis suggests mild opposition.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The programme backed recall of officials but not binding mandates on all elected leaders, so it is left neutral.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The programme favoured social insurance for old age under public arrangements rather than private individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Roosevelt wanted public ownership of water power and conservation of resources but favoured private small holdings of land generally; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legislative control of the budget is not discussed, though the programme works within the constitutional order; inferred mild support.

single-official-language.rationale: Official-language policy is not in the programme, though assimilation was; neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not discussed in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not discussed, though Roosevelt ranked dividends below human character; neutral.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The 1912 programme proposes no covert support for foreign insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed in the 1912 programme, which spoke of honorable dealing with other nations; inferred as split.

corporate-influence.rationale: The central theme of Osawatomie was ending business domination of politics, with campaign limits and lobbyist registration.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the programme's nationalist premise that national government should guard the American public interest against outside and corporate influence; the sources do not address foreign donors.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the platform's social-insurance and family-welfare planks and Roosevelt's national-strength outlook; no birth-rate incentive is stated in the opened sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the programme favoured national over local power and the platform has no limit on who may buy property.

job-guarantee.rationale: The platform sought social insurance and measures against unemployment, but not public jobs for all; inferred from its preference for regulation over state employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: The programme has no theory of democracy and peace; Roosevelt backed arbitration yet also a large navy, so adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Roosevelt demanded respect for law and order but also attacked courts that blocked reform; inferred that obedience was owed to just, democratically made law.

non-intervention.rationale: The 1912 platform and Roosevelt's speeches rest on a strong navy and an assertive national role abroad, which does not fit a rule of absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources back labour organisation and its rights but do not address industrial versus craft structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt attacked "malefactors of great wealth" as a class, not a minority group, and the programme treats all citizens as one nation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the platform's support for the family and its protective measures for women; nothing suggests ending legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The platform demanded publicity of campaign contributions and corporate accounts, from which wider openness of government is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Croly's New Nationalism looks to national integration and national markets, not local self-sufficiency, so adherents would not prefer local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The programme builds permanent national parties, expert commissions and organised labour, and relies on a strong central organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and the stress on national over state power; Roosevelt also backed arbitration treaties, hence low confidence.

religious-nation.rationale: Roosevelt's nationalism defined Americans by citizenship and character, not religion; inferred from the programme's civic framing.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The programme is assertively nationalist, with a strong navy, so tribute to a leading power is inferred to be rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The programme stressed national over state power and uniform standards, so regional revenue-sharing is favoured over local retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The programme accepts private property under regulation and rejects socialism, so common ownership of productive property is refused.

defeat-communism.rationale: The 1910-12 programme predates the Russian Revolution, so there is no stated position.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; the programme backs strong public agencies and social insurance but says nothing on private delivery of public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Roosevelt's programme is secular in content and uses moral language; a materialist view of religion is not part of it, inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Roosevelt held large combinations to be natural and beneficial when regulated, treating industrial growth as a base for reform.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform sought women's suffrage and labor standards by law, treating equality as reachable by legal reform within capitalism.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; the programme's social insurance is unrelated to public housework, so inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purity is not in the programme, and its assimilation aims concern education in English rather than purging words; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The programme favoured national government authority and assimilation of newcomers; treaties with internal nations are not addressed and this is inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme is centred on a strong national government and rejects socialism, and Croly sought national unity rather than small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: The platform proposed distributing and assimilating immigrants, not steering a majority group into minority regions; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The programme presents regulated capitalism as a middle course between unrestricted business and socialism; inferred from its defence of regulation.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; Roosevelt's national progressivism rests on present citizens' welfare rather than ancestral claims, inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1910-12 programme; denial is inferred to be rejected from Roosevelt's stress on honesty and national character.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic: the 1912 programme does not touch the question and adherents of the era would differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme sought more direct democracy through primaries, initiative, referendum and recall, and fought party bosses.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a 20th-century progressive would be disinclined to punish blasphemy, inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Roosevelt's imperial record is outside the profile's scope, and the programme itself is silent on colonial governance.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the programme; no basis to place it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme's reliance on popular will and civil government implies rejecting it, inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme pressed primaries, initiative, referendum and recall to make government answer to the people, though it does not extend to workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The platform addressed labour and women's suffrage separately; adherents did not share an intersectional view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1912 programme; no basis to place it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1912 programme; no basis to place it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Croly and Roosevelt claimed to combine Hamiltonian means with Jeffersonian ends, but did not call left and right obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Roosevelt accepted industrial capitalism and sought to regulate it, not abolish wage labour; the claim is inferred as rejected.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme's immigration plank favoured assimilation, so the claim is inferred as rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The 1912 platform and Roosevelt's speeches place power in the people, not in any divine source.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents had no common line.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The platform's labour and women's-protection planks suggest support, though the issue is anachronistic.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme accepts markets but wants federal regulation and social insurance against sickness, age and unemployment.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The platform and Roosevelt's speeches called for a strong navy and military preparedness.

rich-first.rationale: Roosevelt put human welfare above property and wanted regulation to spread benefits widely, not let some prosper first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Roosevelt favoured an assertive world role and a navy, but the programme does not address blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Roosevelt's programme sought to make government answerable to the people through direct democracy and attacked privilege, so hereditary succession is inconsistent with it; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Roosevelt wanted supervised, not abolished, corporate capitalism and credit; mutual banks are not in the programme, so this is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The programme predates the IMF; its nationalism and its respect for supervised finance make a firm stance unlikely, inferred at low confidence.

property-franchise.rationale: Roosevelt put human welfare over property rights and the platform backed direct democracy and women's suffrage, which is incompatible with wealth qualifications; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The programme backed conservation and women's suffrage but never linked them; adherents would not likely endorse the connection; inferred.

reification.rationale: Roosevelt accepted market concentration under regulation; a critique of reification is foreign to the programme, inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Roosevelt attacked the influence of corporate wealth over politics and public opinion, so adherents would likely accept the claim; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Roosevelt favoured law enforced by courts and commissions, though he also wanted a strong discretionary executive; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The platform's democratic and national-unity principles do not support racial limits on voting, though the 1912 party's record on race was weak; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The platform backed initiative, referendum and recall; online participation is an anachronistic extension of that direct democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Progressives wanted publicity as a remedy for corporate and political abuse; extended by inference to government records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The programme does not address it, but a national, welfare-oriented liberalism would not restrict marriage by religion; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The programme does not address it; its inclusive national appeal makes religious boycotts inconsistent with it; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the programme of primaries, initiative, referendum and recall to make government answerable to ordinary people; the sources never mention assemblies chosen by lot, and the preference for expert commissions pulls the other way.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the Progressive outlook of putting human welfare and present conditions ahead of inherited forms; religious doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Roosevelt's Osawatomie speech attacks the corrupting political power of great fortunes and says government must be freed from special-interest wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme never touched it, and no line can be inferred from its principles.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The programme is moral and reformist and respects religion; state-promoted unbelief is far outside it (inferred).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A strong-government programme that favours order and enforcement of regulation cannot be read as supporting abolition (inferred).

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Croly's national-unity theme favours majority-based national democracy over group shares; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The platform urged state action such as social insurance and labor protection instead of reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Roosevelt himself sought a third term in 1912 yet the two-term tradition was familiar; no programme position, adherents split (inferred).

vote-delegation.rationale: The programme sought direct-democracy tools such as initiative, referendum and recall, but not delegable proxy voting; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources for a position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the programme; no line can be inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1912 platform backed women's suffrage and equality in public life; marital authority itself is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the programme calls for full American citizenship and Americanisation of immigrants rather than a political role for non-citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Osawatomie principle that human welfare comes before property rights; rent caps are not mentioned.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the 1912 platform wants corporations regulated but not property rights in inventions abolished; Roosevelt backed the patent system.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's stress on national service and preparedness and his support for scouting; the platform does not call for drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Roosevelt's preference for military strength and national power.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Croly's and Roosevelt's nationalism, which stresses national sovereignty and strength.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Confession of Faith's moral language on national duty, since formal genocide recognition is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Osawatomie speech puts human welfare above property rights and says labour is superior to capital; the platform pledges to protect workers and tax unearned wealth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the militant, strenuous ethos of Roosevelt's nationalism; non-resistance is foreign to it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Croly's nationalism looks forward to a nation to be built by democratic action, not an ancient identity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; the era's progressivism did not address the construction of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; the 1912 platform backed women's suffrage on the basis of equal citizenship, not a critique of the category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's patriotic honouring of the fallen; the sources do not discuss sainthood language.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Confession of Faith casts the campaign as a crusade: 'We stand at Armageddon, and we battle for the Lord.'

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anachronistic; Croly's nationalism concerns the American nation-state, not a diaspora homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: Croly argues for national action and the state to realise the national promise, rather than cultural renewal first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed, and the platform's moral language is conventionally Protestant.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed, though the platform's support for women's suffrage rests on citizenship, not theology.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the programme speaks of a 'square deal' for all citizens and of assimilation, not ethnic ownership of the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the programme concerns merging regions by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Roosevelt defended workers' right to organise and bargain, but the programme never addressed union independence from the state, so this is inferred from its labour plank.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The programme accepted private property under federal regulation and rejected socialism, so the socialist test is not one it applied; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Progressives often favoured public utilities, but Roosevelt's programme focused on national regulation of corporations rather than local ownership; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: The platform pressed for direct election of senators and popular control, while keeping a bicameral Congress; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Roosevelt accepted private ownership of industry under national supervision and did not propose community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The programme rests on strengthening federal and executive power over states and localities, the opposite of delegates who only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: The 1912 platform called for a living wage and minimum-wage protection for workers, which this statement extends to supporting a family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Roosevelt backed federal food and drug regulation, but speed of approval was not an issue in his day; no clear inference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme's faith in science and expert administration points mildly positive but gives no clear answer.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A strong federal state supervising business would be uneasy with untraceable payments; inferred from its regulatory outlook.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme's demand for publicity and disclosure from corporations pulls one way, democratic reform the other.

person-over-state.rationale: Croly subordinates the individual to national purpose, while Roosevelt put human welfare above property; the two pull against each other.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Roosevelt's Confession of Faith is framed in moral and religious language and calls for human character over property, though it does not state this thesis.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: National supremacy over the states was central, so state or regional powers rest on national authority; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; conservation and efficient scientific management of resources suggests support for new agricultural technology.

dense-cities.rationale: Roosevelt's conservation policy and urban reform give no stated view on density versus suburbs.

racial-group-interests.rationale: New Nationalism stressed a single national American interest and opposed hyphenated divisions, so organising by race would be discouraged; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Roosevelt spoke of pride in American nationality and also of racial vitality, but the programme did not address racial pride as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The 1912 platform called for a large navy and Roosevelt defended using force abroad, so armed forces were not limited to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Roosevelt and Croly's nationalism was a civic, American-democratic ideal built on common citizenship and ideals, not a shared language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The programme wanted direct democracy and equal citizens answering to the whole people, so separate religious electorates contradict it; this is inferred from its democratic reforms.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Roosevelt's concern was domestic corporate power, not foreign plots to break up the country; the programme does not address this and the answer is inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: The platform stressed education and social welfare but did not call for free tuition, and the issue is anachronistic.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Roosevelt's conservation programme relied on federal regulation and public stewardship of natural resources rather than taxes on polluters, and pollution taxes are anachronistic.

future-generations.rationale: Roosevelt's conservation platform held that natural resources must be protected for later generations, and the 1912 platform pledged conservation of resources for the people's future use.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The 1912 platform backed women's suffrage and Progressives often argued women would bring moral and social concern to public life; this is inferred from that reform-era view.

arms-reduction.rationale: Roosevelt championed a strong navy and military preparedness, and the 1912 platform called for building battleships, so deep armament cuts are contrary to it.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Roosevelt favoured vigorous executive discretion in foreign affairs, so a ban on secret agreements is inferred as contrary to his practice.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme regulated corporations and currency but did not address cross-border capital flows, which is anachronistic for 1912.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's insistence on a strong federal government as the sole arbiter over private power.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt prized national strength and the platform backed a strong navy, so conscientious refusal of state wars is far from his creed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 1912 platform backed workers' right to organise and collective action to secure fair conditions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the platform's social-insurance and living-wage aims; tax credits themselves are anachronistic.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: the programme wanted an active, expert-led state and gave no weight to legal borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the programme was national and protectionist and never aimed to remake world economic rules for poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Roosevelt explicitly wanted to expand and use federal power and executive agencies, not dismantle the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: Croly and Roosevelt wanted a single national programme of regulation rather than varied local economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Roosevelt's conservation policy treated natural resources as national wealth to be managed for the people; inferred, not framed in accounting terms.

sacred-nation.rationale: Croly's nationalism made the nation a moral purpose beyond individuals, though it was civic rather than explicitly religious.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a programme that valued self-reliant citizens and offered no student-loan scheme.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the programme stressed national unity over sectional conflict but also curbed the power of wealthy interests.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Confession of Faith's appeal to common human welfare and rights of the citizen.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed in 1910-12; the platform favoured informed public opinion but said nothing on public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The programme never addressed religious truth claims; nothing in the Osawatomie speech or platform bears on it, so this is left neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the programme's use of national government to protect working people and its conservation and country-life concerns; guaranteed prices were not a stated plank.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Roosevelt's insistence on a strong navy and national self-defence, which suggests keeping deterrent strength.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: the Progressive Party presented itself as a national party for all citizens, and Roosevelt's nationalism set the common welfare above class interest.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the programme's use of law to protect women and children from harm.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1912 platform endorsed women's suffrage and protection of working women; equal property rights are inferred from that, not stated.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not an issue for the programme; no basis for a position.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Roosevelt wanted expert federal commissions to regulate business and conservation in advance, and distrusted courts as the main check on property use.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the programme's faith in elected government and direct democracy, with no formal place for hereditary or traditional authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Roosevelt held that property and private use are subject to community regulation and made conservation of natural resources a national duty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: Progressives generally preferred expert, individualised treatment of offenders over rigid fixed penalties; the sources do not address sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the platform's immigration plank on education and assimilation of newcomers and Roosevelt's stress on a single national character.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The 1912 platform backed workers' organisation and protective labour law, so it would oppose banning union-security; inferred from that.

voter-id.rationale: The platform pushed to widen popular participation (primaries, initiative, recall), so new barriers to voting would be opposed; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Roosevelt held to equal treatment of all faiths in a secular federal state; inferred, not addressed in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The programme held that elections are not enough and that government must also serve human welfare against business control, so democracy is not only procedure; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Progressive-era moral attitudes were conservative on this, and the sources do not address it; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic: no position exists and the strong-executive order-keeping bent is offset by Progressive free-speech views.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The platform wanted social insurance and regulation rather than cash replacing welfare, an anachronistic idea; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1912 Progressive platform called for equal suffrage for men and women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Progressive reformers did not blame religion for women's position, and many were religious social reformers; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Roosevelt shared the era's racial-science assumptions, so adherents would not call race a construct; anachronistic inference.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; the platform backed women's suffrage and protective labour laws but no such agencies, and adherents' view cannot be settled.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's view that property rights are subordinate to human welfare, which weakens first-claim ownership as an absolute.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Roosevelt favoured arbitration and international order but was strongly nationalist; the question is anachronistic and adherents would split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Progressive-era modernism; the programme is silent on scriptural literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the 1912 platform's backing of women's suffrage and protection of women workers; indigenous self-government is not addressed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the programme's acceptance of capitalism under regulation; a planned state with nationalised property is outside it.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1912 platform urged direct primaries and direct election of senators, so indirect selection of higher offices runs against its democratic reforms.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the Progressive emphasis on civic equality and the separation of church and state; not addressed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the New Nationalism's single-nation emphasis and Roosevelt's hostility to hyphenated Americanism.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; Roosevelt's era handled territory through diplomacy and force, and adherents have no clear stand.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic: decolonisation lay beyond the programme, and no position can be inferred with confidence.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the programme's embrace of industrial progress and the strenuous life, not simple self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's push for national uniformity and continental expansion; not addressed directly.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's support for national military preparedness among men only, as the norm of his era; anachronistic.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Roosevelt treated the national land as a heritage to protect for future generations; inferred from his conservation stance.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Progressive reform rested on law and expert commissions, so killing without trial is inferred to be rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Its focus is domestic national unity, not sponsorship of kin abroad; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Roosevelt held that natural resources belong to the whole people and called for their conservation against private monopoly.

self-ownership.rationale: Roosevelt put human welfare ahead of property rights, but nothing addresses self-ownership; inferred neutral.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Roosevelt favoured progressive income and inheritance taxes over broad consumption taxes; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Its social insurance proposals were universal in design; targeting at the poorest is inferred to be disfavoured.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: It sought direct democracy such as primaries and recall to bypass party bosses and special interests; inferred as partial agreement.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Its platform and speeches attack special privilege for business and demand that government serve the people.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not addressed; Progressive reformers favoured non-sectarian civic politics; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Its programme embraced modern industrial organisation and expert administration; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The 1912 platform endorsed women's suffrage and equal rights; divorce is inferred from that.

national-resource-control.rationale: Its resource-conservation agenda favoured national control over private monopoly; foreign control is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt held that property is subject to community regulation and that fortunes gained through special privilege are illegitimate, so fair process alone did not settle justice.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred and anachronistic: the programme taxed large fortunes and curbed speculation, so a levy on speculative finance fits its principles, though it never addressed one.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic: the 1910 and 1912 programmes did not frame racial advancement in these terms, and adherents of the time were split between paternalism and indifference.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt attacked courts that struck down social legislation but insisted on lawful reform and obedience to law, so he did not hold unjust laws void.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: the programme stressed work, shorter hours for workers and the dignity of labour, not a mass end to paid work; automation was not an issue then.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt favoured a balance of power among great powers abroad but also American primacy in the hemisphere, so adherents point both ways.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: Roosevelt defended rewards for business ability and enterprise alongside labour's claims, which does not fit a view that labour alone creates value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Osawatomie speech joins a strong national government with putting human welfare above property rights and protecting workers, so patriotism and serving ordinary workers go together.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the programme centred on wages, hours, insurance and corporate regulation rather than identity politics, which was not a distinct issue then.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the programme sought to regulate, not replace, the market under constitutional and democratic government and was hostile to socialism and party rule.

missingStatements.text: Government commissions, not courts, should have the main power to supervise large business combinations.
missingStatements.rationale: Roosevelt held that large combinations are natural and should be regulated by executive agencies and a federal trade commission rather than broken up by courts.

missingStatements.text: Courts' rulings that strike down social-welfare laws should be open to reversal by popular vote.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1912 platform and Roosevelt's Confession of Faith urged limiting court power so voters have final authority on social-welfare questions.

missingStatements.text: Human welfare should be placed above property rights when the two conflict.
missingStatements.rationale: Roosevelt said he was for men and not for property and ranked dividends below human character.

notes: Roosevelt's later and earlier records on race, empire and war are not part of the 1910-1912 programme, so statements about them are low confidence.
